explain.say: In 1952 engineers at MIT showed off the first numerically controlled milling machine, driven by punched tape. Today a CNC machine in Pune, Stuttgart or Nagoya follows a program to cut a part to a few micrometres, again and again. Look at the chain from design to part.

draw.text: CNC machines and G-code: how a computer drives a machine tool

explain.say: A designer draws the part in CAD. CAM software then plans the tool path and writes it as G-code: simple lines of letters and numbers. G00 means move fast, not cutting. G01 means cut in a straight line at the feed rate F. G02 and G03 cut arcs, clockwise and anticlockwise. M03 starts the spindle. Which code moves the tool fastest?

explain.say: G00, the rapid move, for travel through air. Now a real line: G01 X50 Y0 F200 means cut in a straight line to X 50, Y 0 at 200 millimetres per minute. A 50 millimetre move at that feed takes 50 over 200 minutes: 15 seconds. S1000 M03 would spin the cutter at 1000 rpm.

explain.say: How does the machine obey? See the board: the controller sends each axis a command, a servo motor turns a ball screw, and the screw drives the table. An encoder on the motor reports the true position back, so the controller corrects any error. That loop is closed-loop control. Why is that feedback important?

parts.label: Ball screw
parts.ask: What does a ball screw do?

draw.text: Ball screw: rolling balls give smooth motion with no backlash

explain.say: Without it, a heavy cut could push the table off and nobody would know! Wonderful. Real link: 5-axis CNC machines tilt the part too, to carve turbine blades in one setup. Exam tip: G90 means absolute coordinates, G91 incremental, so check which mode a program is in.

parts.ask: What does a ball screw do?

faq.q: How does a CNC machine work?
faq.a: A controller reads a program of G-code, works out the motion for each axis, and drives servo motors through ball screws. Encoders feed the real position back so errors are corrected.

faq.q: What does G01 mean in G-code?
faq.a: G01 is linear interpolation: move in a straight line to the given coordinates while cutting at the programmed feed rate F.

faq.q: What is the difference between G00 and G01?
faq.a: G00 is a rapid move at the machine's top speed, used when the tool is not cutting. G01 is a controlled straight-line cut at the feed rate you set.

faq.q: What does a ball screw do?
faq.a: It turns the motor's rotation into straight-line motion of the table. Balls roll between the screw and nut, so it moves smoothly, precisely and with almost no backlash. A servo motor with an encoder drives it.
Computer-aided manufacturing software takes a CAD model, plans tool paths, speeds and feeds, and writes the G-code program for the machine.
